documentation.rationale: Both halves are weak. Identity is missing (no VIN, title or accident data). Maintenance is a specific, itemised parts list but seller-claimed, with no receipts in the capture. Good exterior and interior photos and a clear option list lift it slightly above bare claims.

condition.rationale: Photos show straight, uniform paint, an intact soft top, healthy-looking tires and a clean oyster interior with only light bolster wear. No fault is stated. Claimed renewal of the water pump, thermostat, oil pan, coils, plugs and rear shocks would be strong if invoiced. Underside, engine bay and cluster were not examined.

price_value.rationale: $18,000 asking is well above the fair value estimate of $12,498–$14,811 (mid $13,877). A 2013 M Sport convertible with 52,106 miles sold for $15,000 on 2026-10-13. The claimed cooling and ignition refresh could justify part of the premium, but only if receipts exist.

mission_fit.rationale: Photo-confirmed 6-speed manual with the naturally aspirated N52. Inside the $10,000–$19,000 ideal band. A profile primary bridge candidate that should resell easily within 6–24 months. Convertible top and cooling items are the reliability questions.

logistics.rationale: The car appears to be in Virginia (plates and inspection sticker), a fly-out and long drive from Carmel. PPI access is not stated, though independent BMW shops are plentiful there. A CA smog check on an out-of-state 2012 car should be feasible but needs confirming.

seller_questions: Can you send invoices showing the date and mileage for the water pump, thermostat and oil pan replacements?
Why was the oil pan replaced? Was there a leak, and was the oil-filter-housing gasket or valve-cover gasket also replaced? If so, when and at what mileage?
Has the coolant expansion tank or upper/lower radiator hoses ever been replaced, and when?
Is the clutch original? Where does it engage, and does it slip in 4th–6th under load?
What are the DOT date codes and brand on the four tires?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, plus a photo of the cluster with the engine running?
Can you send photos of the underside, oil pan area and oil-filter-housing area?
Has the car ever had paint or body work, and is the title clean and in your name?
Has the top ever leaked, or have the top hydraulics or seals been serviced? Are the drains clear?
Will you allow a pre-purchase inspection at an independent BMW shop of my choice before any deposit?
Does the exhaust come with the original BMW part numbers or an invoice, and do you have the stock system?
ppi_focus: Oil-filter-housing gasket and valve-cover gasket seepage. Check the new oil pan seal for leaks.
Electric water pump and thermostat: confirm part dates, scan for cooling faults, check the expansion tank and hoses for age and cracks.
Full DME/DSC/top-module scan for stored and historic fault codes.
Convertible top cycle: hydraulic pump, cylinders, seals, and water-test for ingress into footwells and trunk.
Clutch engagement height, slip test, and dual-mass flywheel noise.
Front thrust-arm and control-arm bushings, front struts, and confirm the rear shocks are new.
Underside corrosion check (East Coast car): subframes, jacking points, brake lines.
Paint meter readings for prior body work. Verify the M Sport and option equipment against the VIN.
Tire date codes and even wear. Alignment check.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: dated invoices for the water pump, thermostat and oil pan, plus a clean history report and title.
Up: a price move toward the comp range (around $15,000) or a clean independent PPI.
Down: refusal to supply the VIN or allow a PPI before money moves.
Down: a branded title, unreported accident damage, active oil-filter-housing or valve-cover leaks, a slipping clutch, or top water ingress found on inspection.
evidence.mission_note: A photo-confirmed manual, naturally aspirated N52 M Sport inside the ideal band fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and should resell easily. Its standing depends on whether the claimed cooling refresh is documented and whether a PPI can be arranged remotely.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes, by photos, a Space Gray over Oyster 128i convertible with a 6-speed manual and M Sport visual equipment, and it appears clean cosmetically. Everything mechanical is seller-claimed. The parts list (water pump, thermostat, oil pan, coils, plugs, belt and pulleys, rear shocks, tires, battery) is specific and directly addresses the N52's main weak points, but no invoices appear in the captured listing. No VIN, title or accident data is given, so identity and history are entirely open. Nothing wrong is observed in the photos. The disclosed oil pan replacement points to a prior leak, and the adjacent oil-filter-housing and valve-cover gaskets are not mentioned. The $18,000 asking price sits above the fair value estimate of $12,498–$14,811 and above the recent $15,000 sale of a 2013 M Sport convertible. The car appears to be in Virginia, so whether a PPI can happen before money moves is still to be established.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, dated invoices for the water pump, thermostat and oil pan, tire date codes, and consent to an independent BMW-shop PPI near the car, then run a Carfax/AutoCheck on the VIN.
